findings.reason: an uncited measurement is not falsifiable, and §30's node cannot reproduce its observation at all without knowing which merge candidate produced it, which is the same defect a prior review raised against §28 and the author acted on.
findings.text: §29's Why states "Measured 2026-10-21 in a population at merge: the id failed 1 of 5 alone runs at main `c7210260`" and §30's Why states "it failed once in a loaded 120-file arm (`-n 12`) at a merge candidate", but neither names the population's run directory, log file or (for §30) revision, while the sibling sections that §29 and §30 sit beside do: §26 names the trial logs and §28 names `gate-final-base.log`, `gate-final-head.log` and `diag-stability.log` in their run directory — so the one observation each new node rests on (a 1-in-5 flake and a once-in-a-loaded-arm failure) cannot be opened, checked, or distinguished from a whole-file run by the node dispatched to repair it

findings.reason: the sentence is the sole justification for the deliverable's mechanism constraint, and it decides between "freeze the clock" and "drop the stamp" before the key that decides between them has been found.
findings.text: §30's Deliverable rejects "adding keys to `_VOLATILE_KEYS`" with the reason "which would hide a real divergence", stated as fact while the same section says "Which key differed is not yet known", and the only top-level per-call clock stamp in the composition the section cites is `"checked_at": _iso(moment)` (reckon/budget.py:2263) — a composition stamp of exactly the class (`composed_at`) that `_VOLATILE_KEYS` already drops, so the stated reason does not follow from the plan's own content and gives the node no criterion for the one step it is asked to perform first

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — both changed sections rest their central measurement on a population that names no run directory, no log file and, for §30, no revision, so a reader cannot open the evidence §29 and §30 are built on.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §29's done-when measures a 20-of-20 foreground pass against a control that adds 3,600 s and must fail; §30's measures a 10-of-10 `-n 12` pass against a control that advances the clock 30 s between the calls, and both name the revision, the literal command, the run-directory log and an `EXIT=` terminator.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections write their gate logs, trials and negative controls under the run directory and the repository tree; no session scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment; §29 and §30 appear only as the plan's own section identifiers, and the symbols the sections name (`_VOLATILE_KEYS`, `_now`, `checked_at`) are existing production names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §30's stated reason for rejecting the simpler route is asserted as fact while the same section says the differing key is unknown, and the only per-call clock stamp in the cited composition is a composition stamp of the class `_VOLATILE_KEYS` already drops.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §29 carries one deliverable (a tolerance in one comparison) and §30 one (the parity case compared at one instant); the extra clauses in §30's done-when are the evidence record for that single goal, in the same shape §26 and §27 already use.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every relationship the changed units carry resolves: `f-tsigah-029` (plan.html:966) and `f-tsigah-030` (plan.html:971) are the open followups for §29 and §30, and neither section declares a `depends-on` on anything absent.
